title: GraphCast (& GenCast) Surpass Physics-Based Global Weather Forecasting in Minutes
whyItMatters: Beat ECMWF’s gold-standard physics weather simulator on 90% of targets in under a minute on one TPU—ushering in operational AI meteorology (extended to ensembles by GenCast in Nature 2024).
summary: Published in Science in November 2023 by Remi Lam, Alvaro Sanchez-Gonzalez, Matthew Willson, Peter Wirnsberger, and the Google DeepMind team, GraphCast trained a multi-mesh graph neural network on 39 years of ERA5 atmospheric reanalysis to produce 10-day global 0.25° weather forecasts in under one minute on a single TPU—outperforming ECMWF’s operational HRES numerical solver on 90% of 1,380 verification targets and improving tropical cyclone track prediction. In December 2024 (Nature), DeepMind’s probabilistic diffusion successor GenCast surpassed ECMWF’s flagship ENS ensemble on 97.2% of targets, permanently transforming operational meteorology worldwide.
technicalHighlights: GraphCast (Science, Nov 2023) outperformed ECMWF’s gold-standard HRES physical solver on 90% of 1,380 atmospheric targets while running ~1,000× faster and more energy-efficiently.
Improved tracking of extreme weather including tropical cyclones, atmospheric rivers, and extreme temperature anomalies without explicit PDE solvers.
Extended to full 15-day probabilistic ensemble forecasting by GenCast (Nature, Dec 2024), beating ECMWF ENS on 97.2% of targets and deployed operationally via WeatherNext.
caveats: Trained on historical physics-based ERA5 reanalysis data (making it dependent on traditional data-assimilation pipelines) and can face out-of-distribution tail risks under unprecedented climate regimes.

scoreRationale.foundational: Demonstrated that learned neural simulators can surpass decades of hand-crafted atmospheric PDE solvers on complex chaotic global fluid dynamics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Reshaped global weather agencies (ECMWF AIFS, NOAA, WeatherNext), renewable-energy forecasting, and disaster preparedness within two years.
scoreRationale.verification: Dual landmark peer-reviewed publications (Science 2023 & Nature 2024), open-sourced code/weights, and live operational verification by national meteorological agencies.
scoreRationale.velocity: Compressed multi-hour supercomputer numerical weather runs into <1 minute on a single accelerator.
